questions.q: Where does a chart widget on a Salesforce dashboard get its data?
options: Directly from the object, bypassing reports
From a source report
From a SOQL query typed into the widget
From a spreadsheet uploaded to the dashboard
questions.explain: Every chart or table widget is built from a source report. The dashboard itself stores no data.

questions.q: You want one big headline number, such as total open pipeline. Which widget type fits best?
options: Scatter chart
Stacked bar
Funnel
Metric
questions.explain: A metric widget displays a single number. Gauges show progress toward a target, and funnels show stages.

questions.q: A report has no grouping. What is the consequence for a chart widget built on it?
options: There is nothing to slice a chart by, so the report needs a grouping first
The chart automatically groups by Owner
The widget will show every record as its own bar
Nothing changes; grouping is optional for charts
questions.explain: Chart widgets slice by a report grouping. A tabular report without groupings gives the chart nothing to divide by.

questions.q: What does the 'View Report' link on a widget do?
options: Deletes the widget
Exports the dashboard as a PDF
Opens the source report so a viewer can drill into the detail
Emails the report to the running user
questions.explain: View Report lets viewers move from the summary to the underlying report.

questions.q: According to this lesson, a Lightning table widget shows roughly how much data?
options: Unlimited columns and rows
Up to 10 columns and 200 rows
Exactly 3 columns
Only the first 5 rows
questions.explain: The Lightning table widget is documented as showing up to 10 columns and 200 rows, drawing columns from the source report type.
